mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, p > 0.05 (t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 100,000 jobs and unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive due to stronger labor market momentum boosting corporate optimism.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals weakening demand for capital goods and corporate earnings compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when trigger occurs (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained inflation acceleration (CPIAUCSL month-over-month growth > 0.5%) over the prior 3 months is associated with a negative S&P 5-day forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes and devalue equities.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when inflation condition is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3%, the S&P 20-day forward return is positive due to expectations of future rate cuts and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when 3-month SMA(CPIAUCSL) > 3% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3% coinciding with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,200K triggers a positive S&P 5-day forward return as labor and housing markets jointly signal economic expansion.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when both triggers are met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (PAYEMS) by over 50,000 in a month is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it indicates consumer demand strength and corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when PAYEMS increases by >50,000 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 2-week moving average of industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110, the S&P 60-day forward return is negative due to persistent supply-side weakness and reduced corporate investment expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when 2-week SMA(INDPRO) < 110 (p > 0.05).
